question: What primary component is included in the peripheral nervous system?
explanation: The peripheral nervous system consists of the somatic and autonomic nerves that branch out from the central nervous system to supply the rest of the body. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T18#GNS222_U3_T18_h1)

question: Why are peripheral nerves more susceptible to physical trauma compared to the brain and spinal cord?

options.A: They lack a protective myelin sheath
options.B: They rely exclusively on passive diffusion for oxygenation
options.C: They run superficially through limbs without bony encasement
options.D: They have a much higher metabolic rate than central structures

explanation: Because peripheral nerves course through the extremities unprotected by the skull or vertebral column, they are easily exposed to mechanical injury and compression. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T18#GNS222_U3_T18_h1)

question: Which connective tissue layer directly surrounds an individual peripheral nerve fiber?
explanation: The endoneurium is the innermost connective tissue layer that closely surrounds individual nerve fibers and their Schwann cell tubes. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T18#GNS222_U3_T18_h2)

question: What is the primary physiological function of the myelin sheath along an axon?

options.A: To generate local anesthetic agents naturally
options.B: To speed up electrical impulse transmission via saltatory conduction
options.C: To prevent the diffusion of neurotransmitters into muscle tissue
options.D: To provide structural blood supply to the axon core

explanation: Myelin acts as an electrical insulator, allowing action potentials to jump rapidly from node to node rather than traveling continuously down the axon length. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T18#GNS222_U3_T18_h2)

question: What term describes a nerve disorder that affects a single nerve trunk, often due to localized trauma or compression?
explanation: A mononeuropathy is restricted to a single nerve pathway, commonly seen in focal compression injuries like entrapment syndromes. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T18#GNS222_U3_T18_h3)

question: Which clinical presentation most strongly distinguishes a generalized polyneuropathy from a focal mononeuropathy?

options.A: Sudden paralysis of a single facial expression muscle
options.B: Acute loss of vision accompanied by severe unilateral headache
options.C: Symmetrical, stocking-glove sensory loss in the extremities
options.D: Localized sharp pain triggered by moving one specific finger

explanation: Polyneuropathies typically affect the longest nerve fibers first, presenting as a symmetrical sensory disturbance spreading upward from the feet and hands. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T18#GNS222_U3_T18_h3)

question: What type of peripheral nerve injury involves complete transection of both the axon and its surrounding connective tissue sheaths?
explanation: Neurotmesis represents the most severe grade of nerve injury where the nerve is completely severed, necessitating surgical repair for any chance of functional recovery. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T18#GNS222_U3_T18_h4)

question: Why is spontaneous recovery rapid and complete in cases of mild neurapraxia?

options.A: Local macrophages quickly clear away the damaged myelin sheath
options.B: Schwann cells rapidly multiply to form new nerve pathways
options.C: Collateral sprouting replaces the blocked segment instantly
options.D: The axon structure is preserved without physical degeneration

explanation: Because neurapraxia only causes a temporary conduction block without breaking the axon, normal function returns as soon as the local ischemia or compression resolves. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T18#GNS222_U3_T18_h4)

question: Which symptom is classified as a negative sensory sign of peripheral neuropathy?
explanation: Numbness and sensory loss represent negative phenomena where nerve signaling is absent, whereas tingling and burning represent positive irritative signs. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T18#GNS222_U3_T18_h5)

question: A patient with chronic peripheral nerve damage presents with dry, shiny skin and non-healing foot ulcers. What underlying mechanism explains these physical findings?

options.A: Rapid regeneration of superficial sensory nerve endings
options.B: Impaired autonomic regulation and loss of protective sensation
options.C: Chronic hyper-stimulation of somatic motor pathways
options.D: Excessive local production of myelin by active Schwann cells

explanation: Autonomic fiber damage alters local sweating and blood flow leading to dry skin, while sensory loss allows repeated unrecognized trauma to cause ulceration. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T18#GNS222_U3_T18_h5)

question: What is the primary purpose of performing nerve conduction studies (NCS) in a patient with suspected neuropathy?

options.A: To analyze cerebrospinal fluid chemistry for infectious agents
options.B: To record spontaneous muscle contractions during physical rest
options.C: To visualize structural tears in the spinal cord meninges
options.D: To measure the speed and strength of electrical signals in a nerve

explanation: Nerve conduction studies evaluate how well electrical impulses travel along a peripheral nerve, helping pinpoint the location and nature of the injury. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T18#GNS222_U3_T18_h6)

question: How does needle electromyography (EMG) differ functionally from nerve conduction studies?

options.A: EMG evaluates central nervous system reflexes instead of peripheral pathways
options.B: EMG measures electrical activity directly within skeletal muscle tissue rather than nerve trunks
options.C: EMG provides immediate imaging of bone fractures compressing nerve roots
options.D: EMG can only be performed under general anesthesia in a surgical suite

explanation: While nerve conduction studies assess the nerve itself, needle EMG evaluates the electrical characteristics of muscle fibers to determine if they have lost nerve supply. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T18#GNS222_U3_T18_h6)

question: Which class of medication is commonly prescribed as a first-line treatment for chronic neuropathic pain?
explanation: Neuropathic pain is driven by abnormal neuronal firing, making medications like gabapentin and amitriptyline much more effective than standard analgesics. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T18#GNS222_U3_T18_h7)

question: A patient diagnosed with painful diabetic peripheral neuropathy asks why standard pain relievers like paracetamol or ibuprofen provide little relief. What is the best clinical explanation?

options.A: Painkillers interact negatively with insulin and worsen blood glucose control
options.B: Over-the-counter painkillers are metabolized too quickly by diabetic livers
options.C: Inflammatory chemicals are completely absent from peripheral nerve tissues
options.D: Neuropathic pain stems from abnormal nerve signaling rather than typical inflammatory pathways

explanation: Standard analgesics target tissue inflammation or general pain receptors, whereas neuropathic pain requires agents that stabilize hyperexcitable nerve membranes. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T18#GNS222_U3_T18_h7)

question: What is an essential self-care practice a nurse should teach a patient with severe peripheral neuropathy affecting the lower extremities?

options.A: Inspect the feet daily for cuts, blisters, and hidden injuries
options.B: Soak the feet in hot water every evening to improve circulation
options.C: Wear tight compression socks continuously without removal
options.D: Walk barefoot indoors to maintain natural foot muscle strength

explanation: Because loss of sensation prevents patients from feeling minor injuries, daily visual and tactile inspection is crucial to catch wounds before they ulcerate. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T18#GNS222_U3_T18_h8)

question: Why is testing bathwater temperature with a thermometer specifically recommended for individuals with peripheral sensory loss?

options.A: Sensory loss makes their skin excessively cold and prone to frostbite
options.B: Their hands cannot accurately gauge thermal intensity, risking severe scalding burns
options.C: Hot water causes immediate permanent demyelination of surface nerve endings
options.D: Thermal sensitivity tests help calibrate their home water heater settings

explanation: Impaired temperature sensation means patients may step into scalding water without realizing it, making objective measurement tools necessary for safety. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T18#GNS222_U3_T18_h8)

question: What severe musculoskeletal complication can result from repetitive, unrecognized trauma in a foot with complete sensory loss?
explanation: Charcot joint destruction occurs when a lack of protective pain and position sensation allows minor, repeated joint trauma to go unnoticed and cause severe structural collapse. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T18#GNS222_U3_T18_h9)

question: Which factor is most critical in determining whether a patient's peripheral neuropathy will improve over time?

options.A: The prompt identification and control of the underlying etiology
options.B: The patient's age and overall physical fitness level
options.C: The immediate surgical removal of all affected nerve trunks
options.D: The complete avoidance of all physical exercise regimens

explanation: Reversing or halting the root cause—such as achieving strict blood sugar control or correcting vitamin deficiencies—is the primary driver for nerve recovery or stabilization. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T18#GNS222_U3_T18_h9)
